note: Registered-vs-published discrepancy at scale, openly-accessible sources only. Deterministic core; harms/routing added 2026-07-13. Pre-registration in PRE_REGISTRATION_harms.md.

prereg_verdicts.claim_H_harms_omission_dominant: REFUTED (pre-reg >=40%; observed 12.1-32.3%). Harms NON-QUANTIFICATION gap (55-88%) IS dominant — weaker related claim SUPPORTED.
prereg_verdicts.claim_R_route_to_registry_table: SUPPORTED for t2d (2.47x) + onc (4.21x); borderline tb (1.96x); REFUTED for malaria (1.67x). All >1.5x directionally. For HARMS numbers specifically the registry table is the route in 55-88% of trials (overwhelming).
prereg_verdicts.claim_C_malaria_tb_coverage_advantage: AXIS-DEPENDENT (pre-registered): SUPPORTED on reporting-pub linkage (66/59% vs 45/37%) and lower non-publication (34/41% vs 55/63%); REFUTED on abstract usability (17% vs t2d 28.5%). Malaria/TB are more open but their abstracts are MORE relative-only/median-only.

non_publication_precision_note.malaria_active_search: 0/15 flagged non-pub trials have an NCT-mentioning paper (bare-NCT PubMed search) — cleaner than T2D (3/9 were published-but-untagged). Higher databank-linkage culture (66%) => absence of link is more likely TRUE non-publication.
non_publication_precision_note.confound: several flagged malaria trials are RECENT (2023-2025); non-publication may be publication time-lag, not permanent. The 34% raw rate is an UPPER bound on permanent non-publication.
non_publication_precision_note.t2d_reference: T2D non-pub precision ~0.67 (databank-miss); malaria plausibly higher but recency-confounded.
